Preserve every current load-bearing claim and add a separate results item for every new load-bearing claim when the proof expands. There is no claim-count cap. Keep final_writeup under 3,000 words and each proof_sketch under 500 words.


Proof-state closure is exact over claimed_resolution, every claim and proof_sketch in results, and final_writeup. If no material correction is required, copy those fields from the parent exactly; do not paraphrase or polish them. Bookkeeping fields may change independently.

  "claims": [
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "A hypothetical counterexample may be assumed to contain the empty set and to have ground set equal to the union of its members.",
      "claim_sha256": "c3344bf066d156aa23809e5683498bd3ec0da5d803b4dbac47ef7c4b6c3fc208",
      "evidence": "Let U be the union of all members. Repeated finite union closure gives U∈F, and restricting the ground set to U deletes only zero-frequency elements. If ∅ is absent, adjoining it preserves union closure and every frequency. An original strict violation d_x<|F|/2 remains d_x<(|F|+1)/2, so the enlarged family is still a counterexample.",
      "idx": 0,
      "search_method": "Direct finite-set proof with the empty-family and one-nonempty-member edge cases checked.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "Equivalent active elements can be identified without changing the number of members or any relevant frequency.",
      "claim_sha256": "59d4bc7f532b4d6eb094f77bc06667132d8a06da644eec090ccb880b1a09aa10",
      "evidence": "Equal incidence columns partition the active elements into classes, and every member contains either all or none of each class. Projection onto one representative per class commutes with union. It is injective because two different members differ on a whole class, and it preserves the frequency of every retained class representative and the number of members.",
      "idx": 1,
      "search_method": "Direct quotient-map proof, including injectivity and frequency preservation.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "If any counterexample exists, then a counterexample containing ∅ and having odd cardinality exists.",
      "claim_sha256": "e21a9ca36b52969d750d6ffe5679973df7cc8efe8f6a1d64b1e1e28856e2ea04",
      "evidence": "First adjoin ∅ as in claim 0. If the resulting size is 2k, remove a smallest nonempty member S. If remaining A,B had A∪B=S, every nonempty one would be a subset of S of size at least |S| and hence equal S, impossible; thus closure remains. Counterexample frequencies were at most k−1 and remain at most k−1<(2k−1)/2. The remainder has a nonempty member because {∅,S} itself cannot be a counterexample.",
      "idx": 2,
      "search_method": "Direct parity-reduction proof with closure after deletion checked case by case.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "A union-closed family containing a singleton satisfies Frankl’s bound.",
      "claim_sha256": "389f55f7af9852480cefee0ba40eff21f04dfead23f4d85a0bea0466ce77837b",
      "evidence": "For {x}∈F, the map A↦A∪{x} sends every member avoiding x to a member containing x. It is injective because removing x recovers A. Therefore no more members avoid x than contain it, giving d_x≥|F|/2.",
      "idx": 3,
      "search_method": "Direct injection proof.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "A union-closed family containing a two-element member satisfies Frankl’s bound.",
      "claim_sha256": "162cfb8ac53fda871a625395b7e5313d04e6aeb5b58a76151e4630d75cbf62bb",
      "evidence": "Partition F into N,X,Y,B according to containment of neither, only x, only y, or both. Union with {x,y} injects N into B, so |B|≥|N|. Hence d_x+d_y=|X|+|Y|+2|B|=|F|+|B|−|N|≥|F|, and one frequency is at least |F|/2.",
      "idx": 4,
      "search_method": "Direct four-cell counting and injection proof.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "Every separating union-closed family on n active elements has an element of frequency at least n; hence it satisfies Frankl’s bound whenever |F|≤2n.",
      "claim_sha256": "4770c67eb0b983c009093b33f1ce7b5132db8a8a79abf2dfe9835035fe835441",
      "evidence": "Order frequencies d_1≤⋯≤d_n. For i<j some member contains x_j but not x_i; otherwise F_{x_j}⊆F_{x_i}, and the frequency order forces equal incidence columns. The union M_i of members avoiding x_i therefore excludes x_i and contains x_{i+1},…,x_n. For i<j, M_i contains x_j while M_j excludes it, so M_1,…,M_{n−1} are distinct. They and the full union X all contain x_n, giving d_n≥n. If |F|≤2n, this is at least |F|/2.",
      "idx": 5,
      "search_method": "Direct canonical-member construction and separation argument.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "For a separating family containing ∅, an exact incidence lower bound is available.",
      "claim_sha256": "ad7d0d7aa8a8e6e0920e5cb600959f4ac32e6c49cae71d1e9d0a360be1dc39c8",
      "evidence": "The distinct members X,M_1,…,M_{n−1} have total size at least n+Σ_{k=1}^{n−1}max(r,k); ∅ contributes zero, and each of the other m−n−1 members has size at least r. Thus T=Σ_A|A| satisfies T≥L=n(n+1)/2+r(r−1)/2+r(m−n−1). For n>1, separation ensures r<n; the n=1 case is immediate and obeys the same formula.",
      "idx": 6,
      "search_method": "Direct incidence double-counting and exact evaluation of the finite sum.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "Frankl’s conjecture holds whenever the smallest positive member of the reduced family has size r≥n/2. In particular, it holds for every family with at most six inequivalent active elements.",
      "claim_sha256": "0eddc4da2f078ae03bbbf860dc6cb9bec2a2c4bb1bebac10da45fbadd147a9d2",
      "evidence": "For the lower bound L, exact algebra gives 2L−nm=(2r−n)(m−n−1)+r(r−1). Both terms are nonnegative when r≥n/2, so average frequency is at least m/2. Conversely, a reduced counterexample has r≥3 by the singleton and two-set results but must have r<n/2 by this argument, forcing n≥7. Hence at most six inequivalent active elements is sufficient.",
      "idx": 7,
      "search_method": "Symbolic integer-algebra verification plus the singleton/two-set case split.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "A normalized separating counterexample with parameters n,m,r must have odd m and satisfy an explicit quantitative lower bound.",
      "claim_sha256": "6839bd7a213c587ef99abc53ba9723b32bcdc1985e713d783d086bff838d60d4",
      "evidence": "Apply the odd-cardinality normalization from claim 2 before quotienting; quotienting preserves m. For odd m, every counterexample frequency is at most (m−1)/2, so T≤n(m−1)/2. Combining this with claim 6 gives (n−2r)m≥n(n+2−2r)+r²−3r. Claim 7 gives n−2r>0, permitting division. Claim 5 also makes a violation impossible for m≤2n, hence m≥2n+1. This proves the stated maximum of the two exact lower bounds.",
      "idx": 8,
      "search_method": "Direct combination of the odd normalization, incidence bounds, and exact integer algebra.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_hard_v1_scratch/hard_union_closed_sets/audit-revision/plain/iter_2/exact_union_closed_audit.py",
      "claim": "Any normalized separating counterexample on seven elements must have at least 25 members.",
      "claim_sha256": "6ac30702a17aa6a79df6ded5545e06f994a2b49aa67b298d7f23e33f6555a59f",
      "evidence": "Claims 3, 4, and 7 force r=3, while claim 8 gives odd m≥21. At m=21, lower and upper incidences both equal 70; equality makes all frequencies 10 and forces M_2={x_3,…,x_7}. Any set containing x_1 but not x_2 would then force the absent X\\{x_2}, so the first two columns coincide. At m=23, 76≤T≤77. If M_2 has size 5, strict column containment forces T=76 and d_1=10, but x_1 can occur only in X and at most five triples. Otherwise M_2=X\\{x_2} consumes the unique excess; closure forces M_5=467 and M_6=457. Fifteen further triples are needed, while the exact checker enumerates only ten compatible with union by M_3=4567. Thus 21 and 23 are impossible and the next odd size is 25.",
      "idx": 9,
      "search_method": "Rigorous equality-case analysis, backed by exact enumeration of the exceptional-case triples and exact incidence intervals.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "Frankl’s bound holds if the family is closed under both unions and intersections.",
      "claim_sha256": "ed7478b5a445c4408199eebdc5b55b11b5a1cdb4abd45f3a7b240cd765a01444",
      "evidence": "Adjoin ∅ if needed and choose an inclusion-minimal nonempty A. For x∈A and any member U avoiding x, U∩A is a proper member-subset of A, so minimality gives U∩A=∅. Therefore U↦U∪A injects members avoiding x into members containing x; set difference by A recovers U. The augmented threshold implies the original threshold as its frequencies are unchanged and its family is no larger.",
      "idx": 10,
      "search_method": "Direct minimal-member injection proof, including the effect of adjoining ∅.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_hard_v1_scratch/hard_union_closed_sets/audit-revision/plain/iter_2/exact_union_closed_audit.py",
      "claim": "Exact enumeration verifies Frankl’s conjecture for every labelled ground set of size at most five and verifies the tight-clean power-set conclusion there.",

      "evidence": "The persisted exact checker decides subsets in nonincreasing size. An inclusion is accepted exactly when its union with every previously included subset was already included, so every leaf is union-closed and every labelled union-closed family occurs once. Counts for n=1,…,5 were 4, 14, 122, 4960, and 2,771,104. It found zero Frankl counterexamples and zero tight clean non-power-set families. Independent exhaustive scanning of all 2^(2^n) assignments reproduced the first four counts and classifications through n=4. The n=0 target case is vacuous because a nonempty member is required.",

      "search_method": "Exact exhaustive integer-bitmask decision tree through n=5, independently cross-checked by all assignments through n=4.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"

      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_hard_v1_scratch/hard_union_closed_sets/audit-revision/plain/iter_2/exact_union_closed_audit.py",
      "claim": "The natural strengthening “every smallest nonempty member contains a Frankl element” is false.",

Thus the smallest member 123 contains only elements of frequency 9<19/2, while the family remains union-closed and has Frankl elements outside that triple.",
      "idx": 12,
      "search_method": "Exact exhaustive ordered-pair union check and integer frequency count for the supplied finite family.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "X={1,2,3,4,5,6,7}; F={∅,123,457,1457,123457,467,2467,123467,567,3567,123567,4567,14567,24567,124567,34567,134567,234567,1234567}; smallest member 123 has frequencies 9,9,9 in a 19-member family."
